author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory page by specialty
summary: The paged HTML veterinarian directory accepts an optional specialty filter carried on the request. It narrows the list to veterinarians holding that whole specialty name, case-insensitively, before paging, and paging keeps the filter. An absent, empty, or whitespace-only value shows the full list; a specialty no vet holds shows an empty list, not an error. No visible control is added.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the directory filtered by a specialty some veterinarians hold lists only those veterinarians
The filter matches the whole specialty name and ignores letter case; a value matching only the start of a name is not a match
Moving between pages keeps the filter in force
No filter, an empty filter, or a whitespace-only filter lists every veterinarian as when unfiltered
A specialty no veterinarian holds lists no veterinarian and is shown normally, not as an error
Without the parameter the directory behaves as before
non_goals: A visible form, dropdown, or other page control for the filter
notes: NG-9 narrowed 2026-08-23 (adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-veterinarian-specialty-filter.md). Filter is a URL contract only. Open questions in PRD: trimming surrounding spaces on a non-empty value; a repeated parameter.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reinstate the machine-readable /vets surface with a specialty filter
summary: The machine-readable /vets surface is reinstated as supported, returning the veterinarians and their specialties, and accepts the same optional specialty filter as the HTML directory: whole-name, case-insensitive. A blank value returns every vet; a specialty no vet holds returns an empty collection as success. The withdrawn REQ-VET-002 id is not reused.
acceptance_criteria: The machine-readable surface returns the veterinarians with the specialties each holds
Requesting it filtered by a specialty some veterinarians hold returns only those veterinarians
The filter matches the whole specialty name and ignores letter case; a value matching only the start of a name is not a match
No filter, an empty filter, or a whitespace-only filter returns every veterinarian
A specialty no veterinarian holds returns an empty veterinarian collection as a successful response, not an error
Without the parameter the surface behaves as before
non_goals: A visible control for the filter
notes: JSON /vets reinstated as a supported surface (NG-9 narrowing, adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-veterinarian-specialty-filter.md). Shares the specialty-matching contract with REQ-VET-001. Open question in PRD: whether this surface should page.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the existing Web controller + cached Repository pattern for the vet directory (system-design.md#contracts). One small adjustment: VetController gains an optional specialty filter applied in memory over the cached full collection, and paging moves from the DB-level findAll(Pageable) to in-memory paging over the filtered list so the filter is applied before paging and preserved across page links. The whole-name, case-insensitive match is placed on the Vet domain type as a predicate, keeping the selection rule out of the controller and unit-testable without the web layer. Blank/whitespace normalization mirrors OwnerController's empty-owner-search handling. Recorded in system-design.md#contracts (VetController/Vet rows and the single-sourced specialty-filter note).
integration_points: VetController.showVetList gains @RequestParam(required=false) String specialty; normalize null/blank via strip() to no-filter, then filter the cached vetRepository.findAll() collection and page the result in memory (PageRequest + PageImpl) so filtering precedes paging
Vet gains a boolean predicate (e.g. hasSpecialty(String name)) matching the whole specialty name case-insensitively over its already-loaded specialties
vetList.html pagination links append the active specialty (when present) so the filter holds across pages; no visible input control is added
addPaginationModel adds the active specialty to the model for the links to read

patterns.description: empty-search normalization to reuse: null/blank lastName -> strip() -> empty means broadest result; mirror this exactly for the specialty value so semantics are identical
getSpecialties() already sorts by name; edge case 1 (stable specialty order) is already satisfied and the same specialty set backs the new predicate

risks.risk: Switching the unfiltered path from DB-level findAll(Pageable) to in-memory paging materializes the whole vet collection each request
risks.mitigation: The vet collection is bounded, read-only, and already cached in full via @Cacheable findAll(); in-memory filter+page adds no DB round-trip and no N+1 (specialties are FetchType.EAGER). Keep both surfaces on the single cached findAll() so the filter lives in one place. If findAll(Pageable) becomes unused, retiring it is optional cleanup (minimal-surface) but not required by this slice

risks.risk: Trimming and repeated-parameter behavior are open questions in the PRD
risks.mitigation: Adopt the PRD's narrowest reading: strip() a non-empty value before the whole-name match (consistent with owner search), and bind a single @RequestParam String (first value wins) since multi-specialty filtering is out of scope

notes: Guardrail: keep the match rule in ONE place (Vet predicate) shared by both surfaces; do not duplicate it in the controller or a repository query. Guardrail: empty/blank/whitespace-only must behave identically to the empty owner search (full list). No visible control (URL contract only). REQ-VET-003 depends on this and reuses the same predicate and normalization.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection: the specialty filter runs entirely in-memory over List.copyOf(vetRepository.findAll()) via Vet.hasSpecialty (equalsIgnoreCase). No SQL/JPQL/derived query is built from the request-derived value on either the HTML (/vets.html) or JSON (/vets) handler; VetRepository has no specialty query. No injection surface introduced.

XSS: the specialty param is echoed only into Thymeleaf @{...} link expressions in vetList.html (pagination hrefs), which URL-encode query-parameter values and render inside an auto-escaped href attribute. No th:utext/unescaped output anywhere; the value is never rendered as page text. Default output escaping stays on, matching security-principles.md XSS control.

JSON surface: showResourcesVetList returns a Vets object serialized by Jackson; the specialty param is used only to filter and is never reflected into the response body. No reflected-content or content-type concern.

Input handling: normalizeSpecialty trims and null-coalesces; an arbitrary string is safe as an equalsIgnoreCase operand and a URL-encoded param. Empty/whitespace-only yields the unfiltered list per contract. No security-critical validation is missing.
Mass assignment: specialty is a scalar optional @RequestParam, not a bound entity/command object; no identifier binding is introduced.
No new dependency, endpoint-exposure widening, secret, or deserialization surface. The reinstated /vets route is a read-only GET consistent with the documented demo baseline.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The method `findFilteredVets(String specialty)` uses the `find` prefix, which in this codebase consistently signals a repository-backed lookup: `findPaginatedForOwnersLastName` in OwnerController delegates to ownerRepository, and the pre-change `findPaginated` in VetController delegated to vetRepository.findAll(Pageable). This new method is purely in-memory — it fetches the cached collection and filters it without touching the repository directly. The `find` prefix will mislead the next reader into expecting a DB call, and will train them to ignore the prefix as a signal. Rename to `filterVets` or `filterBySpecialty` to match what the method actually does.
findings.fix: Rename `findFilteredVets` to `filterVets` (or `filterBySpecialty`) at the declaration (line 98) and both call sites (lines 49 and 78).

findings.description: When no specialty filter is active, `addPaginationModel` sets the model attribute `specialty` to `""` (the result of `normalizeSpecialty` for a null/blank input). Thymeleaf URL expressions include empty-string parameters as literal `param=` tokens; only null values are omitted. All five pagination links therefore render as `/vets.html?page=N&specialty=` when the visitor is browsing the unfiltered directory. The controller handles the arriving empty string correctly (normalizes it back to no-filter), so this is not a correctness defect, but the URLs are visibly noisy and surprising to anyone reading them in a browser or in the test expectations. Fix: in `addPaginationModel`, pass `null` rather than `""` when specialty is empty so Thymeleaf omits the parameter from unfiltered pagination links.
findings.fix: In `VetController.addPaginationModel`, change `model.addAttribute("specialty", specialty)` to `model.addAttribute("specialty", specialty.isEmpty() ? null : specialty)`. The controller's null-to-empty normalization already happens before this point, so the only value that would become null here is the empty string, which Thymeleaf will then omit from the URL.

findings.description: `not(containsString(...))` is written as `org.hamcrest.Matchers.not(containsString("James Carter"))` — fully qualified — while `containsString` and `hasSize` are statically imported at the top of the file. The sibling test class `OwnerControllerTests.java` static-imports `not` (line 42), which is the established pattern. The inconsistency is jarring: a reader will look for a reason the qualification is needed and find none. Add `import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.not;` and remove the fully-qualified prefix.
findings.fix: Add `import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.not;` to the import block and replace `org.hamcrest.Matchers.not(containsString("James Carter"))` with `not(containsString("James Carter"))`.

approved_aspects: Match rule is correctly single-sourced: `Vet#hasSpecialty(String)` is the only implementation of the whole-name case-insensitive test, and the controller delegates to it for both surfaces without duplicating the logic

normalizeSpecialty correctly mirrors OwnerController empty-search semantics: null and whitespace-only values normalize to empty string, non-empty values are stripped — the Javadoc also states the trimming assumption explicitly
findFilteredVets delegates the match entirely to Vet#hasSpecialty and does not re-implement the comparison in the controller — the single-source guardrail is upheld
List.copyOf defensive copy on the cached findAll() result is appropriate: it insulates the in-memory filter from any mutation on the cached collection
Thymeleaf pagination links are switched from string-concatenated URL fragments to idiomatic @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})} syntax — a correct and cleaner form
paginate handles out-of-range page offsets cleanly with the start >= vets.size() guard before subList
Javadoc on hasSpecialty states the single-source contract and the caller-trims assumption without over-specifying; the doc on findFilteredVets correctly characterises its role as orchestration only

The checkJavaFormat Gradle task name was not found during the review run; the build-pass record at line 12 lists format as a passed gate check, so format is accepted on the gate record rather than direct verification
